correctness.rationale: Every nonempty support is attained on an open Euclidean simplex-projection affine cell; the KKT Jacobian annihilates constants. Sorted-level cut decomposition is exactly norming for complete-graph Gini variation. Three-level edge counting gives ab(1+2(n-k)/k), and a concave cut-size denominator is minimized at a boundary count. One selected active vertex realizes the resulting fixed-support maximum; small perturbations inside the cell attain the global maximum. Exact integer finite difference and asymptotic calculation complete the proof. Rational checker independently reproduces 346476 active/cut comparisons, 88 true equality pairs, and 28574 further two-input tests. These finite tests corroborate, but do not establish, the universal statement.

value.rationale: The Gini mean difference measures natural permutation-invariant all-pairs signal dispersion. Sharp two-input stability of the standard simplex projection is relevant to robustness of sparse simplex normalizations; the operator contracts dispersion for individual inputs but expands dispersion of differences from dimension four. The exact finite-dimensional modulus, attained witnesses, asymptotic 2-bound, and extremizing support scale sqrt(2n) give structural information that is not an arbitrary finite computation or a direct substitution from coordinate norm estimates.
